sentences: I measure the river's discharge at the same cross-section every Tuesday morning with a current meter.
I check the staff gauge on the north bank and write the water level in my notebook.
I collect a water sample from the middle of the channel to test turbidity and suspended sediment.
I walk along the left bank and note where the current has undercut the soil.
I record the water temperature at three depths using a handheld probe.
I count the number of riffles and pools along a one-kilometer stretch of the river.
I map the meander bends from last year's aerial photographs to see how the channel moved.
I test the pH and dissolved oxygen levels at the downstream monitoring station.
I note the tributary entering from the east and mark its confluence on my map.
I measure the width of the river from the bridge and compare it with last month's figure.
I check the riparian vegetation on both banks and list the dominant tree species.
I record the time it takes a floating stick to travel between two fixed points.
I sample the bed material with a shovel to classify the gravel and sand sizes.
I inspect the levee on the south side for cracks or animal burrows.
I log the river's stage height at midnight and again at six in the morning.
I follow the dry channel of an oxbow lake and note its distance from the main river.
I measure the electrical conductivity of the water at the estuary during low tide.
I count the fish passing through the fish ladder at the dam each hour.
I trace the watershed boundary on a topographic map and mark the drainage divide.
I record the date when ice first covers the river's surface at the monitoring site.
